title: Polynomial ring in a family of variables, and its universal property
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $J$ a set. The *polynomial ring* $R[x_j:j\in J]$ is the commutative $R$-algebra whose elements are the finite $R$-linear combinations $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^\alpha$ of monomials $x^\alpha=\prod_jx_j^{\alpha_j}$ ($\alpha:J\to\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ finitely supported), with coefficientwise addition and the product determined by $x^\alpha x^\beta=x^{\alpha+\beta}$ and $R$-bilinearity; $R\to R[x_j:j\in J]$, $c\mapsto c\,x^0$, is its structure map. (For $J=\{1,\dots,n\}$ one writes $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.) Universal property: for every commutative $R$-algebra $C$ and every family $(c_j)_{j\in J}$ of elements of $C$ there is a unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[x_j:j\in J]\to C$ with $x_j\mapsto c_j$ for all $j$ (evaluation, $\sum c_\alpha x^\alpha\mapsto\sum c_\alpha\prod_jc_j^{\alpha_j}$); in particular two $R$-algebra homomorphisms out of $R[x_j:j\in J]$ that agree on every $x_j$ are equal.
